chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Murazim ibn Hakim, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: The one performing tamattu' enters Makkah on the night of 'Arafah, and the menstruating woman—until when does tamattu' remain for the two of them? He said: As long as they catch up with the people at Mina.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ الْحَائِضُ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: here, the rite of hajj al-tamattu'
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Mina, the location tied to the hajj rites mentioned here
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: the night preceding the standing of 'Arafah

ai.seo_question: Until when can a late-arriving pilgrim or a menstruating woman still perform hajj al-tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the time limit for remaining within hajj al-tamattu' for a pilgrim who reaches Makkah late, as well as for a menstruating woman. The Imam عليه السلام states that tamattu' remains valid for them so long as they catch up with the people at Mina, indicating a legal threshold tied to the rites of hajj.
